goal: Bound scheduled WebSim and stat-weight stdout/stderr so complete nested sync payloads no longer fill journald/syslog, without changing sync behavior, persisted state, timers, source limits, or literal health status.
userValue: Cloud storage remains available for the equipment simulator and its rollback/candidate evidence instead of being consumed by repetitive job payload logs, while operators still see truthful compact status and counts.
nonGoals: Do not run either expensive scheduled sync as verification.
Do not change source ingestion, timers, job cadence, PostgreSQL state, source limits, public payloads, or equipment behavior.
Do not delete historical databases or backups; old log cleanup occurs only after the bounded runtime identity is deployed and verified.

currentTruth.factOwner: The sync functions persist complete state in PostgreSQL; the two runner scripts own only process progress and terminal summary output.

mustChange: Add one shared pure bounded sync-summary/progress sanitizer with an 8 KiB per-line limit.
WebSim and stat-weight runner stdout must emit compact status, runner, revision, scalar counts, and bounded diagnostic counts instead of nested payloads.
WebSim stderr progress must retain stage/status/duration and bounded scalar counts while dropping nested source payloads and raw error strings.
Tests must prove large nested rows, raw errors, and sentinel values do not reach stdout/stderr.
mustNotChange: No sync function call order, source request, PostgreSQL write, timer cadence, environment limit, exit status, or health-state promotion.
No log suppression that turns partial or blocked into success.
No expensive live sync during candidate smoke.
riskUnknown: Some existing operators or tests may parse the full terminal payload even though PostgreSQL is the durable state owner.
Stage callbacks may emit provider-specific nested details that also need the shared sanitizer.
evidenceRequired: RED/GREEN unit tests for 8 KiB bounds, sentinel/raw-error removal, and truthful partial/blocked status.
Existing WebSim/stat-weight PostgreSQL-only runner and deploy-script suites.
Immutable source/file parity smoke that does not launch the scheduled jobs, followed by bounded synthetic runner output.
Post-deploy journal growth and filesystem verification before log rotation/vacuum.

ownership.factOwner: server/sync_log_summary.py owns bounded terminal serialization; server/websim_sync.py and server/stat_weights_sync.py remain the scheduled runners.

engineeringHealth.reason: The root filesystem reached 92% and the latest journal sample was dominated by these two jobs. The jobs are inactive now, so a pure output correction can be tested without load.

acceptanceEvidence: A large nested WebSim/stat-weight fixture serializes to one JSON line no larger than 8 KiB.
Nested profiles, raw provider payloads, full error text, and sentinel values do not reach stdout/stderr.
Literal verified/partial/blocked status, runner, revision, and scalar counts remain visible.
Existing PostgreSQL-only runner and deployment contracts pass.
No live scheduled sync is launched for verification.
After deployment, source/file identity matches and synthetic output stays bounded before old logs are rotated or vacuumed.

decisionLog.decision: Fix the stdout/stderr owner before reclaiming logs; clearing logs alone would allow the next scheduled jobs to refill the filesystem.

harnessFindings.whatHappened: The two scheduled runners pretty-printed complete nested result payloads into journald/syslog.
harnessFindings.impact: Logs consumed multiple GiB and contributed to a 92% root filesystem hard stop for equipment candidates.
harnessFindings.recommendedAction: Persist full state only in PostgreSQL and emit an 8 KiB bounded terminal summary/progress contract.
